chapter: Cab Calloway, Harlem and New York musicians
title: Jelly Roll's stomps and his claim to have invented jazz
summary: Danny explains that Jelly Roll slowed ragtime into stomps and thought his music the only real jazz, hating the fast tempos of Chick Webb.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: Well, Jelly Roll, you know, played stomp. He slowed down rag, and he called it stomps -- stomp-down. You see, everybody, Eubie Blake, everybody...Joe Jordan... All them people was playing Scott Joplin's legitimate thing. Jelly Roll took it and slowed it down. [SINGS A REFRAIN] It's probably because if you're old and you're a hustler... [SINGS, SNAPS FINGERS] See, that's a stomp-down. [SINGS REFRAIN] And you can see they're gonna like Jelly Roll's music, because if you play... [SINGS FAST TEMPO]... you're all out of breath, and you can't talk to the women, you can't get a drink. A lot... You're choking because your oxygen ain't flowin' right. All of that's involved. Jelly Roll give you a nice [SINGS SWINGING TEMPO]...
Yeah. See? So he'd say, 'Well, that's Swing, that's Jazz. I did it. I started it.' He said he

invented it. He believed that his music was the only music. The rest of it was garbage. He'd say, "Now, Chick Webb and them? Too fast. That ain't supposed to be played like that." You couldn't tell him Lindy-Hop. If he went in there, he wouldn't last two minutes playing that tempo. "Hey, what's going on? Come on, man, liven it up. Liven it up." So that's the difference.
